prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2010 manifesto sets out a progressive plan for a “future fair for all,” rejecting a return to “business as usual” after the financial crisis. It backs active, reforming government to secure recovery, protect frontline services, and renew democracy—while demanding responsibility from the top and fairness for ordinary families.

Economy and finance: Labour will not risk the fragile recovery with immediate cuts. It will more than halve the deficit by 2014 through growth, fair tax changes and savings, not by dismantling services. Frontline spending on childcare, schools, the NHS and policing is protected; efficiency, pay restraint and lower-priority cuts deliver savings. A fairer tax mix includes the 50p top rate, reduced pension relief for the highest earners and a 1p NIC rise (shielding low earners). Deep banking reform (more capital, “living wills,” global levy, bonus controls) and new competition accompany an activist industrial strategy: UK Finance for Growth (£4bn) for SMEs and high-tech firms, a Green Investment Bank, a “patent box,” and support for exporters. Infrastructure plans include High Speed Rail, rail electrification, Crossrail, universal broadband via a modest landline levy, and 100,000 EV charging points.

Jobs, welfare and living standards: Labour prioritises full employment and ends life on benefits: a job or training for young people after six months; a guaranteed job after two years for all long-term unemployed—backed by obligations to take work. The minimum wage will at least match average earnings and a £40 Better Off in Work guarantee ensures work pays. Skills Accounts, expanded apprenticeships, and support for entrepreneurs and small firms (People’s Bank at the Post Office, a Small Business Credit Adjudicator) drive mobility. First-time buyers are helped with a stamp duty holiday up to £250,000, funded by a 5% rate on homes over £1m.

Education: Frontline spending rises. Sure Start expands; two-year-olds get more free nursery places; three- and four-year-olds get 15 hours. A “3Rs Guarantee” delivers one-to-one/small-group tuition for children falling behind. Parents gain power to trigger leadership change in weak schools and up to 1,000 secondaries will join accredited groups by 2015. Every pupil has a personal tutor; vocational routes (Diplomas, University Technical Colleges), advanced apprenticeships and widened HE access underpin social mobility.

NHS and care: NHS funding is protected and reformed around prevention, personalisation and enforceable patient guarantees: 18-week treatment or funded private care; cancer tests within one week; GP choice with evening/weekend access; expanded home and end‑of‑life care; access to psychological therapy. A staged National Care Service begins with free home care for those with the greatest needs (from 2011), caps residential costs after two years (from 2014), and moves to a comprehensive, free system post‑2015. The basic state pension is re-linked to earnings from 2012; flexible working expands; the default retirement age ends.

Safer communities and migration: Police and PCSO numbers are maintained, with neighbourhood teams visible 80% of the time, faster action on anti-social behaviour (including a right to injunctions), stronger family interventions, and Community Payback shaped by local votes. Immigration is controlled through an Australian-style points system—no unskilled migration from outside the EU—and citizenship is earned; English proficiency and fair access rules protect communities and workers.

Green future and culture: Around 40% low‑carbon electricity by 2020; 400,000 green jobs by 2015; clean energy from renewables, nuclear and CCS; “pay as you save” home upgrades; progress toward zero waste; protected habitats, Green Belt, and more woodland. The BBC’s independence is upheld; free museum entry continues; supporter trusts gain a path to own stakes in clubs; post offices and pubs are protected.

New politics and global role: Labour proposes referenda on AV for the Commons and a democratic Second Chamber, fixed-term parliaments, a statutory lobbyists’ register, recall for misconduct, stronger local accountability and open data. Internationally, it backs a clear Afghanistan strategy, a Strategic Defence Review while retaining a nuclear deterrent alongside multilateral disarmament, leadership in an outward-looking EU, the 0.7% aid target in law, and reform of global institutions—advancing security, prosperity and climate action.
